notes.text: WORKFLOW: the multiple-comparison trap. Twelve records of PURE NOISE, with no rhythm of any kind, analysed with identical settings. Every one of them reports a peak period, because a periodogram always returns its largest value. Look at where those twelve peaks land: scattered arbitrarily across the search window, which is what a null result looks like in aggregate. Now imagine you had run only one of these records, picked the most impressive-looking spectrum, and reported it. That is the trap. The more series, windows, or preprocessing choices you try, the more certain it becomes that something will look significant. Decide what you are testing before you test it, and read this next to the arrhythmic negative control.
